geo.label: Fed on hold / policy shock
parts: Macro Stance

Growth is cooling while inflation firms: Q4 GDP rose just 1.4%, badly missing the estimate, as inflation firmed at 3% [[n7052]]. Even Governor Waller now weighs supporting a rate pause if labor data stabilize [[n7302]], so the Fed is not positioned to cushion a policy shock. That shock arrived with the Supreme Court ruling: Trump lifted his replacement global tariff from 10% to 15% [[n7284]] and is weighing new national-security tariffs [[n7427]]. We are bearish on US equity beta, not on the economy.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.43% and the 10Y at 4.03%, a +60 bps 10Y−2Y spread that is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23). Over 20 observations the 2Y fell 17 bps and the 10Y 21 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23). Equities missed the bond bid: the S&P 500 fell 1.04% to 6,837.75 and the VIX jumped 10.06% to 21.01 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
New / Most Important

Monday fused two fears: the Dow tumbled more than 800 points as tariff uncertainty and AI-disruption anxiety roiled markets [[n7347]]. Private credit is the third fault line — Treasury Secretary Bessent said ‘we are concerned’ and is keeping a close eye on the market [[n5548]].
Playbook ✓

Own duration through IEF and TLT and run equity beta below benchmark until the VIX closes back under 20; fund it from software and lenders, not from cyclicals with raised guidance. A 10Y back above 4.24%, its level 20 observations ago, would end the bond trade (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23). A negotiated tariff ceiling plus a strong Nvidia guide would justify re-adding beta.

geo.label: ECB patient / recovery building
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is the relative winner of the US policy chaos: activity is recovering, inflation is below target and equities have outperformed. The STOXX 600 is up 2.97% over 20 sessions while the S&P 500 is down 1.13% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Activity & Inflation

February business activity beat expectations as manufacturing bounced back [[n2392]], and January inflation fell to 1.7% [[n2108]], leaving the ECB free to stay patient rather than tighten. EUR/USD at 1.1835 is down 0.2% over 20 sessions, so the currency is not tightening financial conditions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
New / Most Important

The tariff ruling cuts both ways: EU lawmakers again postponed the vote on the US trade deal after the tariff upheaval [[n3085]], leaving the bloc without a negotiated ceiling. Energy is the standout — European oil and gas stocks hit a record high, surpassing their 2007 level [[n2486]].
Playbook ✓

Overweight Europe versus the US through the STOXX 600 and euro-area energy, and buy dips caused by US tariff headlines rather than by European data. Hedge with DAX puts if Brussels retaliates; the DAX already fell 1.06% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Cut the overweight if the next PMI round falls back below expectations.

geo.label: easing bias / weak demand
parts: Macro Stance

China enters its post-holiday restart with an external windfall and a domestic hole. Bloomberg frames Beijing as a winner as Trump is forced to rejig tariffs [[n0948]], and Trump will travel to China next month with tariffs in focus [[n0812]]. At home, demand remains weak and policy incremental. Net: tactically better for offshore equities, structurally unchanged for growth, hence Mixed rather than Bullish.
PMIs & Activity

The latest official manufacturing PMI, for January, dropped to 49.3 [[n0446]] — a contraction reading at the start of the year and the latest available official print. The February PMI is the confirmation test. Until it moves back above 50, treat activity as soft and dependent on targeted support rather than on organic demand.
Credit Impulse

January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists [[n0601]], so the seasonal surge is not a genuine credit impulse. Benchmark lending rates were left unchanged for a ninth straight month [[n0906]], signalling that Beijing prefers targeted tools to broad rate cuts. A real turn would need loan growth beating forecasts outside the January peak, which has not happened yet.
Property

January new-home prices extended their decline as weak demand hounds the sector [[n6314]]. Without a floor in prices, household wealth keeps eroding, which caps both consumption and mortgage demand. We would need two consecutive months of slower price declines before treating property as stabilising; until then developers and property-linked banks stay an underweight.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The Supreme Court removed the IEEPA layer, but the replacement 15% global tariff [[n7421]] applies to all partners, which narrows China’s relative disadvantage rather than removing it. The planned Trump visit [[n0812]] turns the coming weeks into summit diplomacy, and an unchanged LPR [[n0906]] leaves fiscal policy to do the lifting. Consumption subsidies and larger special-bond quotas are the confirming signals to watch.
Markets & Flows

Hong Kong reopened strongly: the Hang Seng rose 2.53% to 27,081.91 and is up 1.87% over 20 sessions, while ASHR slipped 0.26% to 34.01 and KWEB fell 1.28% to 32.28, down 10.08% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The Shanghai Composite’s last completed session closed at 4,082.07 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). USD/CNY held at 6.9080, down 0.93% over 20 sessions — a firmer yuan that eases capital-outflow pressure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
New / Most Important

The ruling shifts leverage to Beijing before the summit, and Bloomberg’s ‘China wins’ framing [[n0948]] showed up in the Hang Seng’s 2.53% jump in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The flip side is that a 15% universal tariff [[n7421]] still caps export upside, and the internet platforms are not participating: FXI is down 1.93% over 20 sessions and KWEB far more, so money is rotating toward exporters and hardware rather than consumer tech (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Playbook ✓

Own mainland beta via ASHR and Hong Kong exporters into the summit run-up; keep KWEB underweight until it recovers its 20-session loss. Add if February loans beat forecasts and new-home prices stop falling; cut if the Trump trip slips or national-security tariffs [[n7427]] land on Chinese supply chains. ⚠ Divergence: the trade windfall arrives while the official PMI sits at 49.3 [[n0446]] and lending rates are frozen — external relief, not domestic reflation.

geo.label: gradual hikes / reflation
parts: Macro Stance

Japan has strong export momentum: January exports grew nearly 17% on soaring shipments to China [[n0661]]. Core inflation, however, slowed to a two-year low, complicating the BOJ’s hike timing [[n3324]], while a Reuters poll still sees the policy rate at 1% by end-June [[n3296]]. That combination — strong external demand, cooling prices, gradual hikes — is equity-friendly.
Activity & Currency

USD/JPY closed at 154.3390, down 0.53% in the prior session but up 1.02% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The Nikkei 225’s last completed session closed at 56,825.70, up 5.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-20).
Playbook ✓

Stay long Japanese equities with a partial yen hedge while exports stay strong. The tail risk is a sharp yen rally: the US led January rate checks and eyed joint intervention with Japan [[n3392]]. Raise the hedge ratio on any fresh intervention headline; drop it if the BOJ signals a longer pause.

geo.label: hawkish RBA / squeezed consumer
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA hiked in February and sees no set path for future rates [[n0145]]; with unemployment steady at 4.1%, talk of another rise is building [[n0178]]. Policy is tightening into a household sector that is already squeezed, which is a poor mix for domestic earnings.
Demand & Financing

Economic confidence hit a 13-year low [[n0188]], a sign the hike is reaching household demand. AUD/USD rose 0.78% to 0.7111 and is up 2.86% over 20 sessions, while the ASX 200 slipped 0.61% to 9,026.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Playbook ✓

Own AUD against USD on rate differentials — UniSuper calls the currency undervalued and is increasing its hedging [[n0232]] — and stay underweight domestic consumer names. Prefer copper-exposed miners; Rio Tinto just reported record copper production [[n5690]]. Reverse if the RBA signals it is done or the currency’s 20-session gain unwinds.

geo.label: easing cycle / strong growth
parts: Monetary & Activity

Poland pairs fast growth with on-target inflation: GDP accelerated to 4% in Q4 (Bankier: ‘PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent’ — GDP accelerated to 4 percent) [[n3632]], and January CPI, although above forecasts, was within target as economists weigh a March rate cut [[n3646]]. The soft spot is labour: wages grew at the slowest pace in five years and employment fell sharply [[n3797]], which strengthens the case for the MPC to move.
FX & Markets

USD/PLN fell 0.62% to 3.5649 and EUR/PLN held at 4.2199; EPOL rose 0.77% to 38.10 (up 3.28% over 20 sessions) and the WIG20TR ETF gained 1.57% to 68.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Leadership: PKN.WA is up 9.99%, PGE.WA 9.11% and PEO.WA 9.04% over 20 sessions, while DNP.WA jumped 4.1% and KGH.WA 3.34% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). FXMAG says the WIG20 is knocking on record highs, with Dino and KGHM standing out [[n3966]].
Companies

Bank Pekao topped profit estimates on higher fee income [[n3467]], supporting the dividend case for Polish banks even as rates fall. CDR.WA is the laggard, down 9.08% over 20 sessions, and ALE.WA is down 5.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Security & New Development

The EU approved €44 billion in SAFE defence loans for Poland [[n3454]], a multi-year funding line for defence procurement that should flow to domestic suppliers. Warsaw also banned Chinese cars from military bases and barred personnel from connecting phones to them [[n3477]], a sign of tighter security screening of Chinese technology.
Playbook ✓

Own Polish banks (PEO.WA, PKO.WA) and Orlen (PKN.WA) into a likely March cut, using EPOL for USD exposure while EUR/PLN holds near 4.22 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Avoid CDR.WA until a product catalyst; trim if the MPC holds in March. ⚠ Divergence: the WIG20 is near records and GDP runs at 4% [[n3632]], yet wages and employment are weakening [[n3797]] — the market prices the rate cut, not the slowdown.
Narrative

Consensus treats AI as tech’s growth engine; the driver that matters now is AI as a destroyer of software margins. MarketWatch asks whether a single blog post erased more than $200 billion of software market cap [[n5506]], and XLK is down 4.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported

Investors dumped Microsoft despite the largest earnings beat in its history [[n1778]]; MSFT fell 3.21% in the prior session and is down 17.49% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Beats no longer protect seat-based software.
EPS Upside Watch

Upside surprise is likelier where revenue is tied to compute volume rather than seat counts. AAPL is up 7.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23) — the market is paying for hardware franchises that AI does not replace.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The ‘AI winners’ basket is no shelter: ORCL is down 20.24% and PLTR 23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The AI trade is splitting into compute suppliers and everyone else — own the former, underweight the application layer.
Narrative

Communication services is caught between AI capex and AI disruption: CNBC argues the AI debt binge broke the hyperscalers’ ‘unspoken contract’ with investors [[n5492]]. XLC is down 1.37% over 20 sessions, META 3.27% and GOOGL 5.01% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported
Pinterest sank nearly 17% as tariffs hit earnings [[n1721]] — ad platforms with merchant exposure feel trade policy first, and the market punished the miss hard.
EPS Upside Watch

The IEEPA ruling could release ad budgets at cross-border merchants if refunds flow, but the replacement global tariff [[n7284]] limits that tailwind. For Meta and Alphabet the upside surprise investors will reward is capex discipline, not revenue beats.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Streaming is not a safe haven: NFLX is down 11.73% and DIS 5.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Content scale has stopped being a moat the market pays for while AI threatens both production costs and attention.
Narrative

Financials are where AI fear and credit fear meet: XLF fell 3.35% in the prior session, JPM 4.22%, BAC 3.75% and GS 3.25% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Blue Owl anxiety is rattling the $1.8 trillion private credit market [[n5547]], and banks are the visible public proxy.
Reported

No large-cap US bank reported in the window; the information came from Washington instead, where Treasury is keeping a close eye on private credit [[n5548]]. That is not a loss forecast, but official scrutiny raises the cost of capital for lenders and BDCs alike.
EPS Upside Watch

Trading revenue is the offset: the VIX is up 30.58% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), which lifts market-making and favours GS-style franchises over pure lenders. Provisions, not revenue, will decide Q1 numbers.
⚡ Breaking Convention

If the scare stays contained, XLF’s 4.41% fall over 20 sessions is an entry point: banks gain share when private lenders gate funds (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The buy trigger is Blue Owl-style redemption limits [[n5547]] not spreading to other managers.
Narrative

Energy is the market’s cleanest geopolitical hedge: Brent closed at 71.49, up 8.52% over 20 sessions, and XLE is up 12.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). European oil and gas stocks hit a record high, surpassing their 2007 level [[n2486]].
Reported
Occidental jumped as a $5.8 billion debt cut and a dividend hike impressed investors [[n1912]] — the market is paying for balance-sheet repair and cash return, not volume growth.
EPS Upside Watch

XOM rose 2.36% in the prior session and CVX is up 10.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). With Brent well above its 20-session reference of 65.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), Q1 upstream estimates look too low and revisions should follow the strip.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The premium is diplomatic, not physical: oil pulled back as US–Iran talks were set to resume [[n5514]], and Henry Hub gas is down 43.41% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Own integrateds with buybacks rather than pure crude beta.
Narrative

Industrials are the market’s preferred physical-AI expression: the data-centre rush is spurring an earnings windfall for power-gear makers [[n5609]]. CAT is up 20.72%, GE 15.35% and XLI 6.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported
Deere stock jumped after a fiscal-year guidance boost [[n1900]] — a non-AI cyclical upgrade that broadens the sector’s earnings base beyond data centres.
EPS Upside Watch

Power equipment and grid suppliers carry the best revision momentum, because utility capex plans are their order books: PPL’s spending plan jumped 15% to $23B on transmission and grid hardening [[n2041]].
⚡ Breaking Convention
Aerospace lags the capex story: BA is down 8.61% over 20 sessions and 5.15% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Own the electrons, not the airframes, until delivery data improve.
Narrative

Discretionary is losing both the consumer and the AI narrative: XLY is down 6.61% over 20 sessions, AMZN 14.17% and TSLA 10.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Q4 GDP growth of just 1.4% [[n7052]] leaves little cushion for big-ticket spending.
Reported

DoorDash climbed 14%, reversing a plunge after missing on earnings and revenue [[n1821]] — investors will look through misses when growth investment explains them. AMZN fell 2.3% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch

Home Depot and Lowe’s report in the week ahead [[n2023]]. Mortgage rates below 6% [[n6603]] help, but January home sales posted their biggest monthly decline in nearly four years [[n6308]], so turnover rather than rates will set the guides.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tariff refunds after the IEEPA ruling are a hidden margin tailwind for importers, but the 15% replacement levy [[n7284]] claws much of it back. NKE fell 3.53% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23): the market is not giving retailers credit for refunds yet.
Narrative

Staples are the crowd’s AI-proof hiding place: XLP rose 1.23% in the prior session and is up 7.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). That makes them a crowded defensive rather than a cheap one.
Reported

Walmart beat estimates but offered a cautious outlook amid a ‘somewhat unstable’ backdrop [[n1868]]; WMT is down 6.03% over five sessions despite a 2.29% rise in the prior one (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch

Upside sits with volume-led staples that hold price as tariffs shift. COST is up just 0.28% over 20 sessions at 986.02 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), so expectations there are not stretched.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The sector’s bellwether is being sold on guidance while the ETF rallies — a sign the defensive bid is indiscriminate. Prefer selected staples over XLP until Walmart’s cautious tone [[n1868]] is tested by the next print.
Narrative

Healthcare is regaining its role as the earnings-visible defensive: XLV rose 1.1% in the prior session and is up 0.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). UNH, down 20.75% over 20 sessions, remains the managed-care drag (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported

The decisive print was clinical, not financial: Novo’s next-generation obesity shot failed to match Lilly’s drug in a head-to-head study [[n5666]], and LLY jumped 4.86% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch

M&A is the catalyst: Gilead agreed to buy cancer-drug developer Arcellx for up to $7.8bn [[n5667]], validating oncology pipelines. Large-cap pharma with cash will keep buying growth, which supports mid-cap biotech valuations.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Obesity is turning into a single-leader market rather than a duopoly [[n5666]]. That concentrates sector upside — and risk — in LLY at 1,058.56 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Narrative

Materials run on two engines — monetary metals and AI-capex copper: gold closed at 5,225.60, up 4.94% over 20 sessions, and XLB is up 5.98% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Gold rose above $5,200 on tariff uncertainty and Iran tensions [[n5705]].
Reported
Rio Tinto highlighted record copper and bauxite production in its full-year results [[n5690]]. FCX is up 8.51% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch
Gold miners have the cleanest upside: NEM at 124.25 is flat over 20 sessions while gold is up 4.94% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), so margins are expanding faster than the share price.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Copper the commodity is lagging copper the equity: front-month copper is down 2.33% over 20 sessions at 5.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Silver’s 5.15% jump in the prior session shows the metals bid is about hedging as much as industry (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Narrative

Real estate has become an AI-immune income trade: dividend-paying real estate stocks are outperforming as AI fears roil markets [[n5617]]. XLRE is up 5.72% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported

The window’s real-estate news was private capital paying up: multifamily REIT Veris is to be acquired by an Affinius Capital-led group in a $3.4 billion all-cash deal [[n5613]]. Take-privates put a floor under public REIT valuations.
EPS Upside Watch

Funding costs are falling: the 10Y is down 21 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23) and mortgage rates dropped below 6% [[n6603]]. Refinancing savings should lift 2026 guidance at levered REITs.
⚡ Breaking Convention
The risk is transaction volume, not rates: January home sales posted their biggest monthly decline in nearly four years [[n6308]]. Prefer income REITs over transaction-driven residential names.
Narrative

Utilities are now a growth sector priced as one: Bloomberg says AI’s thirst for power has made them a crowded growth sector [[n4882]]. XLU is up 9.68% and NEE 10.91% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported

PPL’s spending plan jumped 15% to $23B on transmission and grid hardening [[n2041]] — rate-base growth is the earnings engine. CEG is up 1.64% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch
Transmission-heavy names with approved plans carry the cleanest upside: regulated returns on a bigger base compound EPS without merchant-power price risk.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Crowding is the risk: VST fell 2.1% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), and a sector Bloomberg already calls crowded [[n4882]] is vulnerable if 10Y yields reverse higher.
Narrative

European autos face weak volumes, Chinese competition and US tariff risk at once: the SXAP tracker fell 1.66% to 45.41 in the prior session and is flat over 20 sessions, with BMW.DE down 2.9% and VOW3.DE 2.54% on the day (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Reported

Europe’s car sales fell 3.6% in January as Dacia plunged and Chinese brands surged [[n5134]]. Stellantis is heading for its first annual loss after EV write-downs [[n5577]]; STLA is down 21.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch
Upside is limited to cost stories; MBG.DE is up 0.66% over 20 sessions, the relative stand-out, while RNO.PA is down 0.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The Supreme Court ruling was supposed to help, yet the EU postponed its US trade-deal vote [[n3085]] and Washington is considering national-security tariffs [[n7427]] — sector-specific levies would hit carmakers first.
Narrative

Semis remain the AI capex toll road: SOXX is up 3.51% and TSM 10.5% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). ASML unveiled an EUV light-source advance that could yield 50% more chips by 2030 [[n5480]].
Reported
Applied Materials gave a rosy forecast as AI and memory boost demand [[n1685]]; ASML is up 6.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
EPS Upside Watch
Nvidia reports on Feb. 25 [[n1774]], and prediction markets are 95% sure of a beat [[n5463]]. MU at 420.97 is up 5.33% over 20 sessions on memory demand (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Breadth is the problem: AMD is down 24.29% and INTC 3.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Own the capacity owners (TSM, ASML) over design challengers until the Nvidia guide clarifies share.

earnings_pattern.title: Guidance beats the quarter — and AI exposure sets the multiple
parts: Rewarded

Raised outlooks and capital returns: Deere stock jumped after a fiscal-year guidance boost [[n1900]], Occidental jumped on a $5.8 billion debt cut and dividend hike [[n1912]], and DoorDash climbed 14% after its miss as investors looked through to growth [[n1821]].
Punished

Beats with cautious guides: EPAM plummeted 20% on a tepid 2026 outlook despite a beat [[n1884]], Walmart was sold after a cautious outlook [[n1868]], and Microsoft was dumped despite the largest beat in its history [[n1778]].
Pattern

The market pays for forward visibility and balance-sheet discipline and de-rates AI-exposed services — IT services, seat-based software — whatever they print. The reaction function is guidance first, AI-disruption risk second, the reported quarter third.
Attention into EPS

Attention is concentrated on Nvidia’s report on Feb. 25 [[n1774]] and on Home Depot and Lowe’s [[n2023]]. With a beat widely assumed for Nvidia, the bar is the guide; for the home-improvement chains it is the housing-turnover outlook.
Playbook

Buy post-earnings dips only where guidance was raised; fade beats that come with cautious outlooks; avoid holding AI-exposed services into prints. Into Nvidia, prefer call spreads over outright stock; into Home Depot, position for a cautious guide.

underowned.title: Rate-sensitive real assets: REITs and housing as mortgage rates break 6%
parts: Attention Gap

Attention is fixed on AI winners and losers, but the 21 bps fall in the 10Y over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23) and mortgage rates below 6% [[n6603]] are a quieter tailwind for real assets. Dividend-paying real estate is already outperforming [[n5617]], yet the story is still told as ‘defensive income’ rather than as a rate-cycle beneficiary.
Exposure & Risk

Express via XLRE, up 5.72% over 20 sessions, with LQD (up 0.78%) as the duration-carry complement (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Risks: turnover, after January home sales posted their biggest monthly drop in nearly four years [[n6308]], and a rebound in the 10Y above 4.24% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23).

underowned.title: Copper miners: the physical bottleneck behind AI and the grid
parts: Attention Gap

While investors debate which software business AI destroys, the copper that wires data centres and grids gets little attention: Rio Tinto reported record copper production [[n5690]], and utility capex plans such as PPL’s jump to $23B [[n2041]] are copper-intensive. Front-month copper is down 2.33% over 20 sessions at 5.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23), so the metal is not priced for that demand.
Exposure & Risk

Own FCX, up 8.51% over 20 sessions, and for European exposure KGH.WA, down 11.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Risks: a hyperscaler capex pause after a weak Nvidia guide, and trade barriers that fragment metal pricing across regions.

crypto.title: Bitcoin breaks lower as ETF demand drains
parts: Market Context

BTC closed at 64,616.74 at the prior completed daily close, down 4.5% on the day and 14.57% over 20 sessions; ETH fell 5.23% to 1,855.50 and SOL 6.08% to 77.75 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Equity proxies are worse: IBIT is down 27.91%, COIN 26.14% and MSTR 24.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
New / Most Important

Spot bitcoin ETFs notched five straight weeks of outflows for the first time since March 2025 [[n1269]] — the institutional bid that carried the last leg has reversed. Strategy keeps adding to a losing position [[n1362]], which makes MSTR a leveraged bet on the next move rather than a hedge.
Playbook

Stay underweight tokens and crypto equities until ETF flows turn positive for a full week and BTC reclaims its 20-session reference of 75,633.55 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Prefer the stablecoin rails over price exposure: Standard Chartered sees stablecoins driving $1 trillion of T-bill demand [[n1343]]. Gold, up 4.94% over 20 sessions, has taken bitcoin’s hedge role (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).

flows.title: Selling America, buying duration
parts: Rates & Dollar

The DXY slipped 0.1% to 97.70 as traders sold US assets on trade-policy risk [[n2725]], yet Treasuries rallied: TLT rose 0.37% to 89.74 and IEF is up 1.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). A 10Y at 4.03% and a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) say the bond market is pricing slower growth, not a fiscal scare (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-23).
Credit Check

Public credit is calm while private credit cracks: HYG slipped 0.16% to 80.87 and is down 0.33% over 20 sessions, while LQD is up 0.78% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). The stress sits in Blue Owl-style vehicles [[n5547]], not in listed spreads; a HYG break lower would be the first sign of contagion.
Portfolio Implication

BofA says US stocks drew their lowest share of global flows since 2020 [[n7096]]: the rotation is out of US equities, not out of risk. Hold IG over HY, keep a non-US equity overweight in Europe and Japan, and treat software-loan exposure in BDCs and private-credit funds as the place the next drawdown starts.

anticipatory.title: Nvidia’s print: a beat is priced, the multiple is not
parts: What Is Priced

Prediction markets are 95% sure Nvidia beats [[n5463]], while Bloomberg warns the stock is so stuck that even blowout earnings may not lift it [[n1997]]. NVDA closed at 191.55, up 4.78% over five sessions but only 2.07% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Conditional Expression

If the guide beats on hyperscaler demand, buy SOXX and the capacity owners (TSM, ASML) and fund it from software. If guidance merely meets, fade semis into strength and rotate to power and grid beneficiaries (XLU, XLI), whose earnings revisions do not depend on one print.
Risk

The risk is narrative: AI-disruption fears drove Monday’s sell-off [[n7347]], and a disappointing guide would validate them across the whole AI complex. A VIX at 21.01 already prices elevated event risk, so hedges are not cheap (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).

anticipatory.title: Iran deadline: oil carries a partial war premium
parts: What Is Priced

Trump set a 10-15 day deadline for an Iran deal [[n2929]], while US–Iran talks are set to resume [[n5514]]. Brent at 71.49 is up 5.52% over five sessions and 8.52% over 20, and gold at 5,225.60 is up 3.55% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23) — a partial, not a full, war premium.
Conditional Expression

If talks fail and strikes follow, own XLE and GLD and hedge airlines and European importers; Brent’s 20-session reference of 65.88 then becomes a floor rather than a target (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). If a deal lands, sell the Brent premium, keep gold as the tariff hedge and rotate into consumer discretionary and oil-importing EM.
Risk

The asymmetric risk is a supply event that lifts inflation just as Q4 GDP growth has slowed to 1.4% [[n7052]] — a stagflation shock for bonds that would break the bull flattening and hit both legs of a 60/40 portfolio.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — beat priced, the guide is the trade
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia reports on Feb. 25 [[n1774]]. Thesis: hyperscaler capex is still rising while the stock has gone sideways, so a guide that confirms demand can re-rate it; with prediction markets at 95% for a beat [[n5463]], the guide, not the quarter, decides the move.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 191.55, up 0.91% in the prior session and 2.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23); the hurdle is breaking the range Bloomberg calls ‘stuck’ [[n1997]]. Risk: a guide that merely meets, or AI-disruption fears spreading to compute budgets; cut on a close below the pre-earnings range.

catalysts.title: $LLY — head-to-head win cements obesity leadership
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Novo’s next-generation obesity shot failed to match Lilly’s drug in a head-to-head study [[n5666]], removing the main challenger to Lilly’s pricing power. Thesis: the market had priced a two-player price war; it now faces a clear leader with share gains ahead.
Price Hurdle & Risk

LLY closed at 1,058.56, up 4.86% in the prior session but still down 0.54% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23) — the re-rating has barely begun. Risks: US drug-pricing policy and a rotation out of defensives if the AI trade recovers; exit if the stock gives back the whole jump.

catalysts.title: $HD — housing turnover outweighs cheaper mortgages
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Home Depot reports in the week ahead alongside Lowe’s [[n2023]]. Thesis: January home sales posted their biggest monthly decline in nearly four years [[n6308]], and big-ticket projects follow turnover, not rates; in a tape that punishes cautious guides, a conservative 2026 outlook is the likely trigger.
Price Hurdle & Risk

HD closed at 376.99, down 3.6% over five sessions and 1.77% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Risk to the short: mortgage rates below 6% [[n6603]] could pull spring demand forward, and IEEPA tariff refunds could lift margins; cover if guidance assumes positive comparable-sales growth and the stock holds.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — retail buys what institutions sell
parts: Observed Attention
Retail investors are piling into Tesla as institutions sell [[n4136]]. TSLA fell 2.91% to 399.83 in the prior session and is down 10.96% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Motivation & Bias
Retail is buying autonomy and robotics optionality and anchoring on past rebounds — classic dip-buying into deteriorating price action, with institutions on the other side of the trade.
Instrument & Risk

Use defined-risk call spreads rather than leveraged single-stock ETFs; TSLA’s 4.22% fall over five sessions shows how fast losses compound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Risk: continued institutional distribution.

retail.title: Raspberry Pi / RPI.L — the AI meme stock
parts: Observed Attention
Raspberry Pi stock jumped 50% in a week in meme-stock mania [[n4090]], making the London-listed computer maker the meme of the AI-hardware trade.
Motivation & Bias
The hook is AI-driven demand for small edge devices, wrapped in momentum chasing and social proof; the bias is extrapolating a one-week move into a structural re-rating.
Instrument & Risk
Cash shares only, with thin derivatives liquidity; size it as a lottery ticket with a hard stop. Risk: the round trip typical of meme spikes.

retail.title: Nvidia / NVDA — the earnings-night lottery
parts: Observed Attention
Prediction markets are 95% sure Nvidia will beat [[n5463]], and the retail conversation centres on the post-earnings move rather than the business.
Motivation & Bias
Retail reads a ‘sure beat’ as a sure rally; the bias is confusing the probability of a beat with the probability of a rally, which Bloomberg doubts [[n1997]].
Instrument & Risk
NVDA at 191.55 is already up 4.78% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Prefer call spreads to naked short-dated calls; the volatility crush after the print is the main risk.

retail.title: Strategy / MSTR — the leveraged bitcoin dip-buy
parts: Observed Attention

Strategy keeps adding to a losing bitcoin position as prices drop [[n1362]], and MSTR remains a retail proxy for BTC: it fell 5.6% to 123.71 in the prior session and is down 24.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23).
Motivation & Bias
Retail anchors on prior cycles and ‘digital gold’ framing and buys the drawdown; the bias is sunk-cost commitment while spot ETFs have bled for five straight weeks [[n1269]].
Instrument & Risk

IBIT, at 36.55 after a 4.87% fall in the prior session, is the cleaner vehicle than MSTR’s leveraged structure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-23). Risk: a break below the latest lows triggers forced deleveraging across crypto equities.
